chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel who said:

Murazim asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) — and I was present with him — about the man who is present (i.e., not traveling) praying in an izar (loincloth/garment) while wearing it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should place a handkerchief or a turban on his neck, wearing it.'

key_terms.إِزَار: Loincloth or lower garment, typically wrapped around the waist and legs.
key_terms.يَتَرَدَّى: To wear or drape (garment loosely or casually).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in a single garment (izar) for a non-traveler?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific fiqh of covering the 'awrah (private parts) for a non-traveling man wearing only an izar, ruling that placing a handkerchief or turban on the neck suffices to cover the upper chest. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability in ritual purity and modesty, distinguishing between the minimum requirements for valid prayer and ideal decorum. The ruling underscores the principle that while the izar covers the lower body, the upper torso must be adequately concealed to maintain the integrity of the prayer posture.
